events.title: Samson destroys the temple of Dagon
Death of Jehoash
events.why: 2 Kings 13:13 records the death of Joash (Jehoash), son of Jehoahaz; Jehoahaz dies in 13:9.

events.note: Three months and ten days (2 Chronicles 36:9).
events.why: Theographic's 3M10D is two units in one; the Bible's three months and ten days, as days.
Theographic's 2.5Y is not a whole number of years; the same, in months.

events.title: The Holy Spirit poured out at Pentecost
events.why: Christadelphian terminology: ecclesia means the assembly of believers; the Holy Spirit is the power of God (Acts 2:17-18).

events.title: The ecclesia grows
events.why: Christadelphian terminology: ecclesia means the assembly of believers; the Holy Spirit is the power of God (Acts 2:17-18).

events.title: Saul persecutes the ecclesia
events.why: Christadelphian terminology: ecclesia means the assembly of believers; the Holy Spirit is the power of God (Acts 2:17-18).

events.title: Jesus tempted in the wilderness
events.note: The adversary (satan) is a delegation of the Jewish leaders, the generation of vipers (Matthew 3:7; 12:34). Having seen his baptism, they come to him in the wilderness of the Jordan valley above the Dead Sea, by Beth-arabah, after his forty days of fasting, and offer him the kingdoms of the land, the tetrarchies of Israel, if he will lead them as their king. Matthew gives the order: the wilderness, the pinnacle of the temple, then a high mountain.
events.why: Christadelphian reading of the temptations, split into its three places; see the journey of the same name.

events.note: Luke 10:38 leaves the village unnamed. Bethany is the working identification from John 11:1, and its placement among the later Judean episodes follows the harmony.
This is a meeting of the chief priests and Pharisees (John 11:47-53), not a recorded visit by Jesus to their council.
Jesus meets the man in Jerusalem and sends him to wash in Siloam (John 9:6-7). The man, not Jesus, is explicitly said to go to the pool. The encounter location within Jerusalem is unknown.
Expanded into individual appearances, including John 21. This spans the forty days before the ascension (Acts 1:3), rather than all occurring on resurrection day.

events.why: Theographic gives only Genesis 25:20; the account of the marriage is chapter 24.

events.title: The Passover and the exodus from Egypt
events.why: Theographic's verses run from Exodus 6:7, through the plagues, which are now their own event.

events.title: Israel encamped at Gilgal
events.why: Theographic's one event for Joshua 4-12 is divided: the camp at Gilgal here, then Jericho, Ai, Gibeon and Merom, Haqor's own events.

added.title: Set on the pinnacle of the temple
added.note: Taken up to Jerusalem and set on the pinnacle of the temple: its south-west corner, where the priest stood to blow the trumpet for the sabbath; the stone inscribed "to the place of trumpeting" fell from it. "Cast thyself down": a sign to the people, answered from Deuteronomy 6:16.

added.title: Shown the kingdoms from a high mountain
added.note: A high mountain: Pisgah, where Yahweh shewed Moses all the land (Deuteronomy 34:1–4), and where Balak took Balaam to view Israel, offering him honour (Numbers 22:17; 23:14). The kingdoms offered are the tetrarchies of Israel; "Get thee hence" sends the adversary away (Deuteronomy 6:13).

added.title: Jesus ministers in the Judean countryside
added.note: Jesus and his disciples leave Jerusalem for Judean country. His disciples perform the baptisms (John 4:2); Aenon in John 3:23 is John the Baptist's location. The lower-Jordan point is a geographical estimate.

added.title: Jesus returns through Sidon
added.note: The critical-text reading takes the return from Tyre through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee through Decapolis. The KJV reads departure from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon. The point represents the district, not a proved visit to the city centre.

added.title: Jesus returns beyond Jordan
added.note: After Dedication Jesus returns to where John first baptized and remains there. Bethany beyond Jordan is a working identification from John 1:28, distinct from Bethany near Jerusalem.

added.title: Mighty works in Chorazin
added.note: Jesus' rebuke presupposes earlier mighty works in Chorazin, but neither an individual episode nor its date or itinerary is narrated. This node records that retrospective evidence without an invented chronological edge.

added.title: Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene
added.note: Near the empty tomb; the Holy Sepulchre vicinity is the working estimate.

added.title: Jesus meets the women leaving the tomb
added.note: On their way from the tomb. A nearby point represents the encounter; its precise position and relation to John's Mary appearance are uncertain.

added.title: Jesus walks to Emmaus
added.note: Jesus joins two disciples on the road and enters Emmaus. The village identification is uncertain; the return to Jerusalem in verse 33 is the disciples' journey.

added.title: Jesus appears to the gathered disciples
added.note: Jerusalem that evening. Reusing the supper-room vicinity is an estimate: the texts do not identify this meeting room as the Last Supper room.

added.title: Jesus appears with Thomas present
added.note: Eight days later. The location is inferred as the disciples' Jerusalem lodging; John does not name the house.

added.title: Jesus meets the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias
added.note: Jesus stands on the shore, provides breakfast and speaks to Peter. The exact beach is unnamed; a northwestern-shore estimate is used in the journey notes.

added.title: Jesus commissions the disciples on a Galilean mountain
added.note: The mountain is unnamed. Its relation to the John 21 appearance is left unordered.

added.title: Jesus leads the disciples out and ascends
added.note: Toward Bethany on the Mount of Olives. Acts 1:3 supplies forty days; Luke's compressed narrative is not used to date the ascension to resurrection evening.

added.title: Jesus appears to Simon Peter
added.note: The disciples report an appearance to Simon before the gathering of Luke 24:36. No setting is described; Jerusalem is a working regional estimate, not an identified meeting site.

added.title: Jesus taken first to Annas
added.note: Estimated in the affluent Upper City, near the high-priestly quarter, for John 18:13-24. No house of Annas has been securely identified.

added.title: Jesus sent to Caiaphas
added.note: Working estimate on the southeastern edge of the Upper City, near the traditional high-priestly site. Matthew 26:57 names the host, not the street or building; this identification is uncertain.

added.title: Jesus brought before the morning council
added.note: Estimated in the Upper City near the high-priestly residences for the morning council (Luke 22:66). The Gospel does not identify its chamber; no route into the Temple precinct is asserted.

added.title: Jesus brought to Pilate
added.note: Herod's western palace is the working identification of the governor's headquarters (John 18:28-19:16; Mark 15:16). The Antonia fortress is an alternative tradition. The exact trial courtyard is uncertain.

added.title: Pilate sends Jesus to Herod
added.note: Estimated at the traditional Hasmonean-palace area in the Upper City for Luke 23:7-12. His presence in Jerusalem is explicit; his lodging is not named.

added.title: Herod returns Jesus to Pilate
added.note: Herod's western palace is the working identification of the governor's headquarters (John 18:28-19:16; Mark 15:16). The Antonia fortress is an alternative tradition. The exact trial courtyard is uncertain.

added.title: Abram rescues Lot; Melchizedek blesses him
added.note: Lot is taken captive from Sodom. Abram pursues the kings from Mamre to Dan, and smites them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus; returning, he is met by Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, and gives him tithes.

added.title: Abraham sojourns in Gerar
added.note: Abraham journeys from Mamre toward the south and sojourns in Gerar, where Abimelech takes Sarah and is warned in a dream.

added.title: Hagar and Ishmael sent away
added.note: At Isaac's weaning Hagar and Ishmael are sent away, and wander in the wilderness of Beersheba until God shows Hagar a well.

added.title: Abraham's covenant with Abimelech at Beersheba
added.note: Abraham and Abimelech swear an oath over a well, and the place is called Beer-sheba, the well of the oath.

added.title: Abraham offers Isaac on Mount Moriah
added.note: From Beersheba to the land of Moriah, the third day, where the temple was later built (2 Chronicles 3:1). Yahweh provides the ram, and swears to bless Abraham's seed, in whom all nations shall be blessed (Galatians 3:16).

added.title: Death of Sarah; the cave of Machpelah
added.note: Sarah dies at Hebron, aged 127, and Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah before Mamre from the sons of Heth: his only possession in the land of promise.

added.title: Isaac sojourns in Gerar
added.note: In the famine Yahweh tells Isaac not to go down into Egypt, and renews the oath sworn to Abraham. Isaac sojourns in Gerar, digs again his father's wells, and goes up to Beersheba, where he too makes a covenant with Abimelech.

added.title: Jacob takes Esau's blessing
added.note: At Beersheba Jacob, by his mother's counsel, receives the blessing of the firstborn, and is sent away to Padan-aram to take a wife of Laban's daughters, out of Esau's reach.

added.title: Jacob's dream at Bethel
added.note: Going out from Beersheba toward Haran, Jacob sleeps at Luz and sees the ladder set up on the earth; Yahweh gives him the land and the promise made to Abraham and Isaac, and he calls the place Bethel.

added.title: Jacob serves Laban for Leah and Rachel
added.note: At the well of Haran Jacob meets Rachel, serves Laban seven years for her, is given Leah, and serves seven more for Rachel.

added.title: Jacob leaves Laban; the covenant of Galeed
added.note: After twenty years Jacob flees with his household; Laban overtakes him in mount Gilead, and they raise the heap Galeed and the pillar Mizpah between them.

added.title: Jacob wrestles at Peniel
added.note: The angels of God meet him at Mahanaim. At the ford Jabbok he wrestles until daybreak and is named Israel, and calls the place Peniel: I have seen God face to face.

added.title: Jacob meets Esau and settles at Shechem
added.note: Esau runs to meet him and they are reconciled. Jacob builds a house at Succoth, then comes to Shechem, buys a field, and raises an altar, El-elohe-Israel.

added.title: Dinah and the men of Shechem
added.note: Shechem the son of Hamor defiles Dinah; Simeon and Levi slay the men of the city.

added.title: Jacob returns to Bethel
added.note: Jacob's household put away their strange gods; at Bethel God appears to him again, confirms the name Israel, and renews the promise of the land.

added.title: Jacob goes down to Egypt
added.note: At Beersheba God tells Jacob, Fear not to go down into Egypt; I will go down with thee. Joseph meets him in Goshen, and he stands before Pharaoh, a hundred and thirty years old.

added.title: The burning bush at Horeb
added.note: Keeping Jethro's flock, Moses comes to Horeb, the mountain of God, in Midian; Yahweh declares his name, I AM THAT I AM, and sends him to bring Israel out of Egypt.

added.title: Moses before Pharaoh; the plagues
added.note: Moses returns from Midian, meets Aaron at the mount of God, and asks Pharaoh to let the people go; the plagues fall on Egypt, and Goshen is spared.

added.title: Crossing the Red Sea
added.note: Led by the pillar of cloud by the way of the wilderness of the Red sea, Israel camps before Pi-hahiroth and passes through the sea on dry ground; Pharaoh's host is drowned. The song of Moses.

added.title: The bitter waters of Marah; Elim
added.note: Three days without water, then the bitter waters of Marah made sweet by the tree; then Elim, with twelve wells and seventy palm trees.

added.title: Manna in the wilderness of Sin
added.note: The people murmur for bread; Yahweh gives quails at evening and manna in the morning, and the sabbath rest.

added.title: Water from the rock; Amalek at Rephidim
added.note: Moses smites the rock in Horeb and the place is called Massah and Meribah; Joshua defeats Amalek while Aaron and Hur hold up Moses' hands.

added.title: Jethro visits Moses at the mount of God
added.note: Jethro brings Zipporah and her sons to Moses where he camped at the mount of God, and counsels him to appoint judges.

added.title: The spies sent from Kadesh
added.note: Twelve spies search the land as far as Hebron and the brook Eshcol; ten bring an evil report, and the generation is turned back into the wilderness for forty years. Joshua and Caleb alone are spared to enter.

added.title: Water from the rock at Meribah; Miriam dies
added.note: In the first month of the fortieth year, at Kadesh, Miriam dies; Moses smites the rock twice and is barred from bringing the congregation into the land.

added.title: Aaron dies on Mount Hor
added.note: Aaron's garments are put on Eleazar his son, and Aaron dies in the top of the mount, by the border of Edom, aged 123.

added.title: Sihon and Og overthrown
added.note: Israel takes Heshbon, the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, and smites Og king of Bashan at Edrei.

added.title: Balaam blesses Israel
added.note: Balak brings Balaam to the high places of Baal, to the top of Pisgah and to the top of Peor to curse Israel camped in the plains of Moab; he blesses them three times, and foretells the Star out of Jacob.

added.title: Moses' words in the plains of Moab
added.note: On this side Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses declares the law again, and gives Joshua the charge to lead Israel over.

added.title: Jericho falls
added.note: Seven days round the city, the seventh day seven times; the wall falls flat, and Rahab and her household are saved.

added.title: Ai taken; the covenant at Ebal
added.note: Achan's sin brings defeat at Ai; after judgment in the valley of Achor, Ai is taken by ambush. Joshua builds an altar on mount Ebal and reads the law, half the people over against mount Gerizim.

added.title: Gibeon; the sun stands still
added.note: The Gibeonites gain a league by deceit; the five kings of the Amorites besiege Gibeon, and are chased by the way of Beth-horon while the sun stands still upon Gibeon.

added.title: The northern kings at the waters of Merom
added.note: Jabin king of Hazor gathers the kings of the north at the waters of Merom; Joshua smites them suddenly and burns Hazor.

added.title: The tabernacle at Shiloh; the land divided by lot
added.note: The congregation sets up the tabernacle at Shiloh, and Joshua casts lots before Yahweh for the seven tribes that remain; he is given Timnath-serah in mount Ephraim.

added.title: Joshua's covenant at Shechem
added.note: Joshua gathers the tribes to Shechem: choose you this day whom ye will serve; as for me and my house, we will serve Yahweh.

added.title: Samuel born and called at Shiloh
added.note: Hannah of Ramathaim-zophim prays at Shiloh for a son and lends him to Yahweh; the child Samuel ministers before Eli, and Yahweh calls him in the night.

added.title: The ark among the Philistines
added.note: The ark is carried from Ebenezer to the house of Dagon at Ashdod, then to Gath and Ekron, plaguing each; the kine bring it back to Beth-shemesh, and it rests at Kirjath-jearim twenty years.

added.title: Samuel judges Israel at Mizpeh
added.note: Israel puts away the Baalim at Mizpeh; the Philistines are thundered upon, and Samuel sets up the stone Ebenezer. He judges Israel year by year in circuit to Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpeh, returning to Ramah.

added.title: Saul anointed by Samuel
added.note: Seeking his father's asses, Saul comes to Samuel's city in the land of Zuph and is anointed. His signs: two men by Rachel's sepulchre at Zelzah, three at the plain of Tabor, and the company of prophets at the hill of God.

added.title: Saul made king at Mizpeh; Jabesh-gilead saved
added.note: Saul is chosen by lot at Mizpeh; he relieves Jabesh-gilead from Nahash the Ammonite, and the kingdom is renewed at Gilgal.

added.title: Jonathan at Michmash
added.note: Saul offers the burnt offering at Gilgal without Samuel; Jonathan and his armourbearer climb to the Philistine garrison at Michmash, and the host flees.

added.title: Saul rejected after Amalek
added.note: Saul spares Agag and the best of the spoil, sets up a monument at Carmel, and at Gilgal Samuel tells him, to obey is better than sacrifice: Yahweh has rejected him from being king.

added.title: David anointed at Bethlehem
added.note: Samuel anoints the youngest son of Jesse, the shepherd, in the midst of his brethren.

added.title: David flees from Saul
added.note: From Naioth in Ramah to Nob and the shewbread, to Achish at Gath, the cave Adullam, Keilah, the wildernesses of Ziph and Maon, and En-gedi, where David spares Saul's life.

added.title: David at Ziklag
added.note: Achish king of Gath gives David Ziklag; the Amalekites burn it while he is away, and he recovers all.

added.title: Saul and the woman of Endor
added.note: With the Philistines gathered at Shunem, Saul goes by night to a woman with a familiar spirit at Endor.

added.title: David king in Hebron
added.note: The men of Judah anoint David king in Hebron, where he reigns seven years and six months; then all the tribes come to him there.

added.title: David takes Jerusalem; the ark brought up
added.note: David takes the stronghold of Zion, the city of David, and brings up the ark from Baale of Judah, that is Kirjath-jearim, dancing before Yahweh.

added.title: David and Bathsheba; Nathan's parable
added.note: While Joab besieges Rabbah, David takes Bathsheba and has Uriah slain; Nathan tells him, Thou art the man.

added.title: Absalom's revolt
added.note: Absalom is made king in Hebron; David flees Jerusalem over the Kidron and up the mount of Olives, weeping, past Bahurim where Shimei curses him, to Mahanaim, where he hears of Absalom's death.

added.title: The threshing floor of Araunah
added.note: After the numbering of the people and the pestilence, David buys the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite and builds an altar: mount Moriah, where the temple was built (2 Chronicles 3:1).

added.title: Solomon anointed at Gihon
added.note: Adonijah exalts himself at En-rogel; at David's word Zadok and Nathan anoint Solomon at Gihon, riding on the king's mule.

added.title: Solomon's dream at Gibeon
added.note: At the great high place of Gibeon Solomon asks for an understanding heart, and is given riches and honour also.

names.why: A word of the name, Lot, finds Lot himself; TIPNR has no record of his daughters.
Ptolemais is Acco (Acts 21:7), as in journeys.json.
